conf.description: cisco-asa device-admin dataset, syslog-raw format (605xxx logins, 611xxx auth results, 502103 privilege change, 111009/111010 executed commands): parsing is deferred entirely to the Elastic cisco_asa integration, which has its own dissect pattern per message. This pipeline is intentionally thin: it only tags event.dataset and passes _raw through untouched.

conf.comment: cisco-asa / device-admin / syslog-raw: insider-threat and change-control evidence. Do NOT re-parse username/Uname, sockets, service, interface, cmd, or privilege-level here -- the Elastic cisco_asa integration owns the per-message-ID dissect for this family, including the server.user.name vs source.user.name identity split (an Elastic-side @custom-pipeline step per the map). The field table's only transform (message_id lookup) needs a field already extracted from the body, so it is not safely implementable pre-parse. The map's Cribl-side recommendation to redact secrets in 111009/111010 command strings targets the parsed 'cmd' field, which this thin pipeline does not extract; redacting against raw, unparsed _raw risks corrupting the command syntax the integration needs, so it is left as a follow-up @custom pipeline gap (see README) rather than guessed here.
